subject: Request vs derived data: default retention behavior — clarification for BrightBank procurement
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@brightbank.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on default capture: requests, prompts, generated outputs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to confirm a few things about your default capture/retention behavior before we proceed with the security questionnaire. Two specific clarifications would be great: 

1) By default, does Redwood retain the raw request payloads (the exact text sent by our app) and the raw responses the model returns, or are those considered transient by default?
2) How do you treat user-provided prompts that are used as context (PII vs non-PII) vs generated outputs derived from those prompts — are generated outputs treated differently for retention/exports?

We'd like to avoid listing anything inaccurate in our internal compliance docs. If you have a brief summary and any supporting doc we can attach to our procurement packet, that would be ideal.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Director, Procurement — BrightBank
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture: requests, prompts, generated outputs

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions and for pulling the procurement team in. Looping in Marissa (product) and Karthik (security & privacy) as they own the canonical language we share with customers.

At a high level: Redwood's hosted API captures request/response artifacts by default to support observability, billing, and model quality monitoring. That said we make explicit distinctions between categories (requests, prompt-context, generated outputs, and derivatives) and we provide customer controls and enterprise opt-outs.

Marissa/Karthik — can you share the short summary and the annotated doc Elena can attach to BrightBank's packet? Ideally a one-page explanation and the PDF we've been using for procurement.

Jonas
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@brightbank.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture: requests, prompts, generated outputs

Hi Elena — thanks for the patience. Attached is a concise summary (redwood-default-retention-summary.pdf) and a simple data map (brightbank-data-map.xlsx) that we typically provide to procurement/security teams. Below is the plain-language summary you can paste into your docs: 

- Default capture: By default, Redwood stores the request payload (what the customer sends to the API) and the corresponding model response. These are retained for observability, billing, and to detect regressions or abuse. Default retention window depends on the plan: hosted (30 days), dedicated (90 days), private (customer-managed).

- Prompt vs. prompt-context: "Prompts" (explicit user-supplied text that forms the input) are treated as part of the request payload. If a prompt contains PII you consider sensitive, customers can use client-side redaction or the API's sensitive-field masking before sending.

- Generated outputs and derivatives: Generated outputs (model responses) are stored by default as part of the response artifact. Derivatives — items created by processing outputs (ranked lists, embeddings, feature vectors) are classified separately; some derivatives (embeddings) are stored in long-term stores for features unless the customer opts out.

- Ephemerality options & controls: Customers on Hosted can opt out of storing request/response artifacts by enabling the "no-persist" flag at the request level; for Dedicated/Private customers there are contract/config settings to shorten or eliminate retention. We also provide an admin-level automated purge (schedules) and an on-demand deletion API for covered artifacts.

- Export and deletion semantics: When a customer requests deletion, we initiate a deletion workflow that removes artifacts from primary stores and triggers TTL tombstones for analytic stores; full propagation can take up to 7 days. For EU residency customers, data is kept in-region and deletion propagates to regional replicas per the same workflow.

- Auditability & evidence: We can provide an export of artifacts we retain for your account (if you have the right contract) and an attestation that deletion workflows were executed. The attached PDF outlines the retention windows and opt-out APIs we expect most customers to use.

If you'd like, Karthik can add a short paragraph on secure keying and how we avoid storing encryption keys with artifacts.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Data Governance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-default-retention-summary.pdf (PDF, 132KB)
Attachment: brightbank-data-map.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)
From: Elena Park <elena.park@brightbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on default capture: requests, prompts, generated outputs

Marissa, Jonas — this is perfect and exactly what procurement needs. A couple of quick follow-ups for our legal team: 

- Can you confirm the exact API flag name for request-level no-persist so we can include it in our tech spec?
- For Dedicated customers who want zero retention, is there a standard contract addendum, or do you treat that as a case-by-case engineering config?

If you can drop the API string and a short sentence on contract approach (or attach a standard addendum template) we'll be ready to move to the SOW step.

Thanks,
Elena
On Mon, Jun 26, 2028 at 08:25 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick answers to Elena's legal follow-ups: the request-level flag is `persist=false` on the request (we also accept `x-redwood-persist: false` header). For Dedicated customers, we have a standard addendum that can be included in the MSA (zero-retention appendix); engineering also performs a configuration review to ensure no downstream analytics copies are enabled. I'm copying Karthik for the attestation language.
> 
> - Marissa
